doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Playing with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band
summary: Mullins describes how he came to join Al Vollmer's band and how easy it is to work with.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well let me see now, this June it’s been about oh maybe five or maybe six months. We kind of got into lock with each other. Let me see, how did it happen? The gentleman that formed the band, Al Vollmer, he’s a physician, dentist. And somehow or another me and him, we sort of, I guess you might say bumped each other. You know.

And he just liked the way I played. And we got together. And it’s been a very easy band, very easy and what I might say — professionally exciting band playing with these guys. When I get on the bandstand with them it’s never no, lot of friction or a lot of, you know, blah-blah-blah stuff going on. It’s always for all we know we’re there to play music. And that’s what everybody does, with the intention of trying to sound and play as well as they can.
